headline.text: Herzog picks Eisenkot to form Israel's government
headline.context: Netanyahu was passed over after the October vote.
headline.vo: Israel's president has chosen opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, not Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, to try to form the next government.

beats.label: of 120 lawmakers recommended Eisenkot
beats.vo: Sixty-seven of the hundred and twenty lawmakers recommended Eisenkot, including Arab-led parties. Forty-six backed Netanyahu. Eisenkot is a former military chief.

beats.title: What happens next
beats.vo: The October twenty-seventh election left neither side with a majority. On Saturday, President Isaac Herzog announced his choice. The formal handover is on Sunday evening. Eisenkot then has twenty-eight days, with a possible extension, to win sixty-one seats.

beats.quote: Now is the time for the formation of a national emergency government
beats.vo: Eisenkot called for a broad emergency government. Netanyahu wants a national unity government instead, and some of Eisenkot's allies oppose relying on Arab-led parties.

title: Israel's president picks Gadi Eisenkot over Netanyahu to form the next government
caption: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a government after 67 of 120 lawmakers recommended him, against 46 for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The formal mandate is handed over on Sunday. Eisenkot then has 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension, to build a coalition of at least 61 seats.
